left.title: Judge blocks Trump admin's anti-transgender health rule just hours before it was to go into effect
left.body: The Trump administration’s regulation that would have eliminated protections for transgender people from Obamacare has been blocked for now by a federal judge, just hours before it was set to go into effect. NBC News reports the judge “indicated he thought the Trump administration’s so-called transgender rule is invalid in light of the Supreme Court ruling in June on a case involving similar issues in the context of job discrimination.” “When the Supreme Court announces a major decision, it seems a sensible thing to pause and reflect on the decision’s
left.roundup: On Monday, a federal judge blocked a Trump administration regulation that would have rolled back Obama-era anti-discrimination laws regarding access to healthcare for transgender people. The regulation was set to take effect Tuesday; on Monday, U.S. District Court Judge Frederic Block barred the regulation from being enforced until the case could be heard in court. Block cited a similar Supreme Court ruling from June that involved transgender job discrimination as evidence that this other regulation could be invalid. Coverage of this story was generally consistent across left- and center-rated outlets; as of Tuesday afternoon, there was little coverage of this story from right-rated outlets.

center.title: Trump rule on transgender health blocked at the 11th hour
center.body: A federal judge blocked the Trump administration on Monday from enforcing a new regulation that would roll back health care protections for transgender people. Finalized days after the Supreme Court barred sex discrimination against LGBT individuals on the job, the regulation from the federal Department of Health and Human Services was to have taken effect Tuesday. right.title: Federal courts side with transgender people in health care and sports disputes
right.body: Transgender people saw two major breaks in federal court cases Monday over health care access and the ability to play in women’s sports. A federal court in New York halted the Trump administration’s move to roll back health care protections under the Affordable Care Act for transgender people, while another federal court in Idaho issued an injunction against a state law banning transgender women from women’s sports.
